subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: How is the safe bearing capacity of a rock foundation determined from its UCS?
options: Determined solely from the colour of the freshly exposed rock surface
Based on UCS and rock mass quality. Safe bearing capacity = UCS/FOS
Equal to the uniaxial compressive strength with no factor of safety
Governed only by the grain size and never by rock mass quality
solution: BC: higher for massive granite (>10 MPa), lower for shale (<1 MPa). Plate load test.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In mylonites, the asymmetric tails of lozenge-shaped mica fish are used to determine what?
options: Feldspar porphyroclasts with asymmetric recrystallized tails set in a fine-grained mylonitic matrix
Quartz ribbons with undulose extinction in a mylonitic fabric
Lozenge-shaped mica in mylonite. Tails extend in shear direction. Asymmetric shape = shear sense
Garnet porphyroblasts with inclusion trails recording their growth history
solution: Mica fish: bookshelf sliding. Fractured mica flakes. Chlorite-mica fish.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the hardness of the mineral gypsum on the Mohs scale of hardness?
solution: Gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) — hardness 2. Can be scratched by fingernail.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Marble, a nonfoliated metamorphic rock, is the product of metamorphism of which parent rock?
options: Shale
Limestone
Granite
Sandstone
solution: Limestone recrystallizes into marble under metamorphism.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An opencast block of 20000 m² has 30 m of overburden above the seam. The overburden volume to be removed is:
options: 0.06 million m³
0.6 million m³
1.2 million m³
0.3 million m³
solution: Volume = area × depth = 20000×30 = 600000 m³ = 0.6 million m³.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The Wilson cycle is the plate-tectonic model of the repeated opening and closing of ocean basins. It proceeds through which sequence of stages?
options: Only a single episode of ocean opening followed by permanent closure, never repeated in Earth history
The repeated cycle of continental uplift and erosion that progressively flattens all mountain belts
The formation and destruction of continental crust by mantle plume melting alone, without plate motion
Rifting → Spreading → Subduction → Collision (orogeny). Complete cycle of ocean opening and closing
solution: Wilson cycle: Atlantic (opening), Tethys (closing → Himalaya). Supercontinent cycle.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The assembly of the supercontinent Pangaea took place during which geological interval?
options: Occurred during Carboniferous-Permian through collisions
Completed during the Cretaceous period through seafloor spreading
Took place in the Precambrian before the Cambrian explosion
Achieved in the Cenozoic by closure of the Tethys Ocean
solution: Pangaea assembled ~335-299 Ma.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In palynology, palynomorphs include which types of organic-walled microfossils?
options: Only pollen and spores produced by seed plants and vascular cryptogams
Only the organic-walled resting cysts of marine dinoflagellate plankton
Only vegetative hyphae, which survive acid digestion better than any reproductive body
Pollen, spores, dinoflagellate cysts, acritarchs, fungal spores
solution: Palynomorphs: acid-resistant organic microfossils. Used for biostratigraphy, paleoenvironment.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Trilobites became extinct at the end of which geological period?
options: Permian period
Cambrian period
Silurian period
Cretaceous period
solution: Trilobites: appeared Cambrian, diversified through Paleozoic, extinct at Permian-Triassic extinction ~252 Ma.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Lateritic nickel deposits, such as Goro and Murrin Murrin, develop by what process?
options: Ultramafic rocks weathered → Ni concentrated in saprolite and limonite. Goro, Murrin Murrin
Vein-type mineralization filling fractures with nickel sulfide and nickel arsenide minerals in granitic country rock
Hydrothermal replacement of dolomitic host rocks by nickel carbonate and silicate ore
Magmatic sulfide segregation of nickel from mantle-derived basaltic magma
solution: Ni-laterite: New Caledonia, Indonesia. Limonite (Fe-Ni) + saprolite (Mg-Ni silicate).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Isochron method in Rb-Sr dating determines:
options: Age and initial 87Sr/86Sr simultaneously
Only the absolute age of the analysed sample
Only the initial strontium isotope composition
Neither the age nor any isotopic ratio of strontium
solution: Isochron: slope = e^(λt) - 1 gives age, intercept = initial 87Sr/86Sr. Multiple minerals plotted.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Quartzite, a very hard and resistant rock, forms by metamorphism of which parent rock?
options: Metamorphosed limestone with recrystallized calcite and dolomite mineral crystals
Metamorphosed sandstone. Quartz grains recrystallized. Very hard, resistant
Metamorphosed shale whose foliation is defined by aligned clay minerals
Coarse-grained igneous rock composed largely of quartz and alkali feldspar
solution: Quartzite: fracture through grains (not around). Orthoquartzite: >95% quartz.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A kelyphitic reaction rim surrounding garnet indicates what in the rock's history?
options: Decompression during exhumation
Prograde metamorphism to higher temperatures
Injection of hydrothermal fluids along fractures
Shallow burial and sedimentary diagenesis
solution: Kelyphite: symplectite rim (pyroxene + spinel + plagioclase). Forms when garnet becomes unstable during decompression.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What caused the Cretaceous-Paleogene mass extinction event that occurred about 66 million years ago?
options: Chicxulub impact. 75% species extinct (non-avian dinosaurs). Iridium anomaly
Triassic-Jurassic boundary event caused by the eruption of the Siberian Traps
Eocene thermal maximum with deep-sea warming and benthic foraminiferal extinction
Permian-Triassic crisis linked to the emplacement of the Central Atlantic Magmatic Province
solution: K-Pg: Deccan Traps + impact. Alvarez hypothesis. Iridium layer worldwide. Mammals radiated.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An oxbow lake forms through which process of river development?
options: River meander cutoff
Glacial erosion of a bedrock valley
Blocking of a river by a volcanic dam
Subsidence of a tectonic graben floor
solution: Oxbow: cutoff meander loop. Neck cutoff or chute cutoff. Becomes isolated lake, eventually fills with sediment.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A talus cone at the base of a cliff is an accumulation of fallen rock formed by:
options: A gently sloping apron formed by river deposition at the valley floor
A steep cone of wind-blown sand accumulating on the leeward side
Accumulation of fallen rock at cliff base. Angle of repose 35-40°
A flat bench of residual soil formed by in-situ rock weathering
solution: Talus: scree. Grain size decreases downslope. Rockfall shadow: probabilistic runout.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The Fry method of strain analysis, based on center-to-center grain distances, yields which quantity?
options: S-C fabric defined by schistosity and shear band foliations
Mica fish whose asymmetric tails record the sense of shear
Center-to-center distance of grains. Finite strain ellipse from initially random distribution
Rf/φ method applied to deformed elliptical objects such as ooliths, pebbles and reduction spots
solution: Fry: nearest neighbor method. Rf/φ: deformed elliptical objects (ooliths, pebbles).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Threshold hillslope model: slope angle controlled by:
options: The rate of tectonic uplift alone sets the maximum stable slope angle
The rate of fluvial erosion alone sets the maximum stable slope angle
Rock strength and weathering rate, not just uplift rate
The climatic regime alone sets the maximum stable slope angle
solution: Threshold slopes: maximum stable angle. Uplift > erosion → steepening until failure.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Famous layered mafic intrusions include Bushveld, Stillwater, and Skaergaard; their cyclic units and cumulus phases formed by what process?
options: Bushveld (S. Africa), Stillwater (USA), Skaergaard (Greenland). Cyclic units. Cumulus phases
Felsic intrusions composed of granite and syenite that show no internal layered structure at all
Volcanic rocks erupted as thick regional flood basalt successions
Hypabyssal sills and dykes with chilled margins and no cumulate layering
solution: Layered: rhythmic layering, graded, inch-scale. Chromitite (Bushveld). PGE reefs (Merensky, J-M).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The water table in an unconfined aquifer is at what pressure condition?
options: Is at atmospheric pressure
Is at hydrostatic pressure
Equals piezometric surface
Is below the aquifer
solution: Water table: surface where P = Patm.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The trigonal crystal system is treated as a subdivision of which larger crystal system?
options: Monoclinic system, with a single two-fold axis and inclined c-axis
Cubic system, with four three-fold axes along the body diagonals
Orthorhombic system, with three mutually perpendicular two-fold axes
Hexagonal system (rhombohedral axes)
solution: Trigonal: rhombohedral lattice. Quartz, calcite, garnet. 3-fold symmetry.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Cooling joints in a basaltic lava flow typically form in which pattern and in what orientation?
options: Columnar joints in basalt. Polygonal (hexagonal). Perpendicular to cooling surface
Planar joints in sandstone formed by regional compression acting parallel to the bedding planes
Irregular cooling cracks in granite that always follow pre-existing mineral cleavage planes
Vertical joints in shale formed during loading and compaction of the sediment pile
solution: Columnar: Giant's Causeway. Cooling contraction → tensile fractures. ≤1m diameter columns.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The geodynamo that sustains Earth's magnetic field operates by convection in which region of the planet?
options: Convection in liquid outer core. Dynamo action generates dipole field
Surface processes. Weathering of iron-bearing rocks generates the observed dipole field
Inner core. Solid iron crystallisation alone powers the entire geomagnetic field
Mantle only. Convection in the solid lower mantle sustains a permanent magnetic field
solution: Geodynamo: convection of liquid iron in outer core. Self-sustaining. Reverses periodically.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: What is the age range and economic importance of the Cuddapah Supergroup of peninsular India?
options: Proterozoic (1.6-0.6 Ga). Vindhyan also. Cuddapah: Pb-Zn deposits (Zawar)
Archean (3.4-2.5 Ga) greenstone belts with the Sargur group rocks of the Dharwar craton
Cenozoic (66 Ma to present) shelf deposits with prolific hydrocarbon source rocks
Mesozoic (Triassic-Jurassic) coal-bearing rift sequences of the Satpura basin
solution: Cuddapah: Papaghni, Chitravati groups. Vindhyan: Semri, Kaimur, Rewa, Bhander.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: The storage coefficient of a confined aquifer typically ranges between:
options: Typically 10^-5 to 10^-3
Typically ranges from 10^-1 to 10^0 in storage
Typically ranges from 10^-8 to 10^-6 in storage
Typically takes a constant value close to 1.0
solution: S = Ss * b. Very small for confined (elastic storage).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Space group: combination of point group symmetry + translational symmetry:
options: 32 groups. The space groups are identical in number to the crystallographic point groups
14 groups. Space groups correspond exactly to the fourteen Bravais lattices
230 groups. The space groups are exactly equal in number to the point groups
32 point groups × 14 Bravais lattices + glide planes + screw axes = 230 space groups
solution: Space group: complete description of crystal symmetry. International notation: e.g., Fd3̄m (diamond).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: U-Pb concordia diagram: discordant zircons plot below concordia due to:
options: Initial Pb contamination at the time of crystallization
Uranium gain during later hydrothermal activity
Analytical errors with no geological meaning
Lead loss during metamorphism or weathering
solution: Discordia: mixing line between original age and Pb loss event. Upper intercept = crystallization age.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which textural and depositional features characterize the alluvial fan facies from proximal to distal?
options: Fine-grained, well-sorted mud with abundant marine fossils and bioturbation throughout
Carbonate platform facies with reefs, ooids and lagoonal muds in a warm tropical sea
Thick evaporite sequences deposited in a restricted, hyper-arid basin with no clastic input
Coarse, poorly sorted. Proximal (debris flow) to distal (sheet flood, sieve)
solution: Alluvial fan: arid/semiarid. Debris flows, stream channels. Bajada: coalescing fans.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: In Landsat 8, Band 10 is acquired by which instrument and is used primarily for measuring what surface property?
options: The OLI (Operational Land Imager) with visible and near-infrared bands
TIRS (Thermal Infrared Sensor). Surface temperature measurement
The OLI panchromatic band, providing 15m high-resolution imagery data
A SWIR band measuring the 1.55-2.29 μm wavelength range of the spectrum
solution: Landsat 8: Band 10 (10.6-11.19 um). 100m resolution (resampled to 30m).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A 3 m seam over 4 km² (density 1.4 t/m³) has a recovery factor of 0.85. The mineable reserve is about:
solution: Mineable = area×thickness×density×recovery = 4M m²×3×1.4×0.85 ≈ 14.3 Mt.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Transform plate boundary: relative motion of plates is:
options: Vertical (upward and downward movement of the plates)
Convergent (plates moving directly toward each other)
Horizontal (sliding past each other)
Divergent (plates moving directly away from each other)
solution: Transform: conservative. No creation/destruction of lithosphere. San Andreas Fault.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A mineral has passed through 3 half-lives of an isotope whose half-life is 4.5 (in the given time units). Its age is:
options: 18 (three times the half-life)
solution: Age = number of half-lives × half-life = 3×4.5 = 13.5.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Oxide copper resources are most amenable to which processing method?
options: In-situ leaching (SX-EW processing)
Direct smelting of the carbonate-hosted oxide ore
Gravity tabling of dense malachite and cuprite grains
Dry magnetic separation of the ferruginous oxide fraction
solution: Oxide Cu: soluble in sulfuric acid. Heap leach or in-situ.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: At a station the S-wave arrives 20 s after the P-wave. Using ~8 km per second of S–P delay, the epicentral distance is about:
options: 320 km
20 km
160 km
80 km
solution: distance ≈ (S−P time) × 8 km/s = 20×8 = 160 km.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Seismic refraction: requires velocity to increase with depth.
options: A low velocity layer gives a strong head wave arrival
Head waves appear even when the lower layer is slower
First arrivals always from faster layer below
The head wave always arrives before the direct wave
solution: Refraction: requires V2 > V1. If velocity decreases, no refraction arrival. Shadow zone.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Compare seismic body waves: how does a P-wave differ from an S-wave in particle motion and speed?
options: S: compressional, faster (6 km/s). P: shear, slower (3.5 km/s) in crustal rocks and sediments
Both waves travel at the same speed regardless of rock density and modulus
P: compressional, faster (~6 km/s in crust). S: shear, slower (~3.5 km/s in crust)
P-waves are shear waves that always arrive after the slower surface waves
solution: P: pushes/pulls. S: shears. P/S ratio: granite ~1.7, sandstone ~1.6-1.8. S can't travel through liquid.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which statement comparing seismic waves is correct?
options: Both P- and S-waves travel through all states of matter
P-waves are slower than S-waves because they compress the medium
S-waves travel faster than P-waves but only as surface motion
S-waves cannot travel through liquids, but P-waves can
solution: Shear (S) waves need a solid; compressional (P) waves pass through solids, liquids and gases, and are faster.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A P-wave travels at 7 km/s and arrives 20 s after the earthquake. The (approx.) distance to the source is:
options: 70 km
140 km
20 km
0.4 km
solution: distance = velocity × time = 7×20 = 140 km.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Mineral exploration: geophysical methods for massive sulfides:
options: Gravity surveys are the sole method capable of detecting sulfide bodies
Seismic reflection alone, because sulfides produce no electrical contrast
Radiometric methods, because sulfide orebodies contain no magnetic minerals
EM (electromagnetic), IP (induced polarization), magnetics
solution: Massive sulfides: conductive (EM), polarizable (IP), magnetic (pyrrhotite, magnetite).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Paleomagnetic dating of rocks relies on matching the recorded magnetic polarity to the:
options: Magnetic polarity reversals. GPTS (geomagnetic polarity time scale). Correlation of magnetozones
Radiometric ages of co-existing igneous minerals and volcanic glass in the beds
Fossil dating of the contained faunal and floral assemblage within the strata
Geochemical correlation of the enclosing sedimentary strata and their marker beds by trace-element fingerprinting
solution: GPTS: Cande and Kent. Chron C1n to C34. Polarity chrons, subchrons. Marine magnetic anomalies.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which term describes the planar fabric (cleavage, schistosity, gneissic banding) developed in metamorphic rocks?
options: Planar fabric in metamorphic rocks (cleavage, schistosity, gneissic banding)
Linear alignment of elongate minerals such as amphibole and sillimanite in deformed rocks
A set of parallel fractures with small displacement developed during brittle deformation
A bedding-parallel fabric inherited unchanged from the original sedimentary layering
solution: Foliation: preferred orientation of minerals. Parallel to axial plane of folds.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: A 6 m seam over 2 km² (density 1.4 t/m³) has a recovery factor of 0.75. The mineable reserve is about:
solution: Mineable = area×thickness×density×recovery = 2M m²×6×1.4×0.75 ≈ 12.6 Mt.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: An aquifer has hydraulic conductivity 10 m/day and a hydraulic gradient of 0.05. The Darcy velocity is:
options: 1 m/day
10 m/day
200 m/day
0.5 m/day

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which features of the zeolite group of hydrated alumino-silicates make them useful as molecular sieves?
options: Hydrated alumino-silicates. Open framework. Used as molecular sieves
Cyclosilicates that form isolated six-membered ring structures without water
Chain silicates with single and double chain anion groups
Sheet silicates with continuous tetrahedral layers and water
solution: Zeolites: large cavities with H2O. Ion exchange, catalysis. Natural and synthetic.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which of the following correctly describes the process and product of spheroidal weathering of jointed rocks?
options: Cracking caused only by repeated heating and cooling of the rock surface
Mechanical disintegration of the rock without any chemical alteration of minerals
Chemical dissolution confined strictly to open joints and fractures
Corners of joint blocks rounded by chemical attack. Concentric shells
solution: Spheroidal: in jointed rocks. Water penetrates joints, attacks from all sides. Corestones.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which spatial interpolation method weights sample points by inverse distance, so closer points have more influence, using a power parameter?
options: Kriging: a geostatistical method with a fitted variogram and best linear unbiased estimate
Inverse Distance Weighted. Closer points have more influence. p = power parameter
Spline: a surface that passes smoothly through all the sample points, with exact interpolation
Natural neighbour: interpolation weighted by Voronoi cell areas, producing smooth surfaces
solution: IDW: d^-p. p=2 common. No uncertainty estimate. Kriging: geostatistical, best linear unbiased.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which seismic wave arrives first and which causes the most damage?
options: Only a single wave type exists, travelling at the speed of light through the crust of the earth
Surface waves arrive first and are the least damaging of all seismic waves
P-wave (compressional, first). S-wave (shear, damaging). Surface waves (Love, Rayleigh)
S-waves travel through fluids fastest and arrive before all other waves
solution: P: 5-7 km/s in crust. S: 3-4 km/s. Surface waves: most destructive (slow, large amplitude).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Peralkaline rhyolite: molar (Na₂O+K₂O)/Al₂O₃ > 1. Mineralogy:
options: Muscovite-rich mineralogy with primary quartz and potassic feldspar
Sodium-rich amphibole (riebeckite), aegirine, no primary muscovite
Calcic plagioclase, augite and hypersthene in a quartz-poor assemblage
Olivine, orthopyroxene and chromite typical of ultramafic cumulates
solution: Peralkaline: excess alkalis over Al. Riebeckite, aegirine. Pantellerite (Fe-rich), comendite.

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Which rock types together constitute the typical lithological assemblage of the Dharwar Craton?
options: Only massive granite with no volcanic or sedimentary supracrustal components preserved anywhere in the craton
Greenstone belts (volcanic-sedimentary) + gneiss (TTG — tonalite-trondhjemite-granodiorite) + granite
Only banded iron formations (BIF) without any associated volcanic or gneissic units in the terrain
Only platform carbonates and evaporites laid down on a stable continental shelf margin
solution: Dharwar: Sargur Group (3.4-3.0 Ga) + Dharwar Supergroup (3.0-2.5 Ga).

subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
stem: Sedimentary rock color: red = iron oxide (hematite, oxidizing). Gray = reducing conditions. White =:
options: Iron-rich sediment deposited under strongly reducing conditions
Leached or very pure (quartz, limestone)
Volcanic ash-rich sediment with abundant ferromagnesian minerals
Organic-rich mudstone with high pyrite and total organic carbon content
solution: White: clean quartz sandstone, pure limestone, kaolinite. Absence of coloring agents.
